ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-1: Zero-price trade via computeRatioX96 overflow returning 0, bypassing pricing bounds in validateHandlerOrder
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: computeRatioX96 returns 0 on overflow, but validateHandlerOrder's pricing bounds check catches it when minSqrtPriceX96 != 0 (since 0 < min triggers revert). When bounds not configured, check is skipped — by design. Halmos symbolic check found no counterexample in 43 paths. Forge test confirms bounds enforcement.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-2: Direct-swap handler bypassing hook pricing bounds due to flag dependency between CLOB and AMMStandardHook
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOB's _enforceTokenHooks calls validateHandlerOrder which checks pricing bounds. Direct swaps go through AMM's beforeSwap/afterSwap which also enforce bounds via _getOrFetchTokenSettings. Both paths enforce pricing independently. Flag dependency is at pool creation (AMM validates hook flags) not at swap time. No bypass path found.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-3: Settings sync gap — setTokenSettings passes raw settings (not memSettings with initialized=true) to hook sync, causing stale cache
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: setTokenSettings passes raw settings to hook.syncTokenSettings, but _getOrFetchTokenSettings auto-corrects by fetching from registry when cache is stale or uninitialized. Self-healing mechanism means at worst one transaction uses stale settings, then next call refreshes. Gas waste only, no economic impact. Forge test confirms self-healing behavior.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-4: Transient storage slot DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT not cleared between hook calls, enabling stale read
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Known as HOOK-001/CP-001. AMM calls beforeSwap per-token, second write intentionally overwrites first. afterSwap only reads the last-written value. By-design behavior documented in audit memory. Forge test confirms overwrite pattern is intentional and not exploitable.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H1: feeOnTop manipulation via unsigned field in SWAP_TYPEHASH — drain extra tokens beyond signed limit
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: feeOnTop excluded from SWAP_TYPEHASH but limitAmount (signed field) caps total exposure. FeeHelper:53 reverts if feeOnTop > amountIn for input swaps. AMMModule:2171 checks total against limitAmount for output swaps. Attacker cannot extract value beyond what signer authorized via limitAmount.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H2: Cosigner bypass when cosigner == address(0) — forge permits without cosigner validation
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: When cosigner is address(0), _validateCosignature skips validation — intentional design for permits that don't need cosigning. The cosigner field IS signed in the permit, so signer explicitly chose no cosigner. No auth bypass.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H3: CLOB order nonce manipulation — replay or forge order IDs
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: nextOrderNonce is auto-incrementing (nextOrderNonce++), stored in contract state, not caller-controlled. Order IDs are sequential and non-reusable. closeOrder checks maker==msg.sender. No way to forge or replay order nonces.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H4: validateHandlerOrder has no access control — attacker calls directly to manipulate pricing
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Function is view-only (doesn't modify state), called by CLOB's _enforceTokenHooks during settlement. Even if called directly by attacker, it only returns validation result — no state change possible. Pricing bounds enforced when configured.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H5: Permit replay across chains or pools — double-spend via missing domain separator binding
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: PermitC uses EIP-712 domain separator with chainId and verifyingContract. Bitmap nonces consumed on use (one-time for fill-or-kill, cumulative for partial-fill). Cross-chain replay impossible due to domain separator. Same-chain replay impossible due to nonce consumption.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H6: Hook settings desync between registry and hook cache — exploit stale settings window
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: _getOrFetchTokenSettings auto-corrects by fetching from registry when cache is stale. setTokenSettings calls hook.syncTokenSettings to push updates. Even if cache is temporarily stale, next beforeSwap call refreshes it. No exploitable window — at worst, one transaction uses stale settings, then self-heals. Gas waste only.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H7: Transient storage slot collision between hooks — exploit overwrite for stale read
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Known HOOK-001/CP-001. DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT overwritten per-token during beforeSwap (AMM calls beforeSwap for each token). Second write intentionally overwrites first. afterSwap only reads the last-written value. By-design behavior.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H8: CLOB order front-running / sandwich attack — manipulate fill price
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOB orders filled at maker's specified price (not market price). Attacker cannot manipulate fill price. depositToken/withdrawToken require maker==msg.sender. openOrder price set by maker. traverseCLOB fills at order prices in linked-list order. No MEV extraction beyond normal priority ordering.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H9: Partial fill permit amount tracking manipulation — over-extract via cumulative cap bypass
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: PermitC uses cumulative fillable amount tracking — _checkAndUpdateRemainingFillableQuantity ensures total filled never exceeds permitted amount. Bitmap nonce with REUSABLE_COSIGNATURE_NONCE=0 allows reuse but cumulative cap prevents over-extraction. Amount tracking is in PermitC (audited, external).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H10: Pool type address validation bypass (6 leading zero bytes) — register malicious pool type
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMM validates pool type addresses at pool creation (must have 6 leading zero bytes). Enforced in lbamm-core, not in hooks-and-handlers. CREATE2 vanity address mining required — not an auth bypass in handler layer. Pool type registration is admin-only in core.
